children: Bayer AG (XETR:BAYN) struck a €3bn deal selling minority stakes in its contraceptives unit to Apollo-led funds and KKR while retaining control, won FDA approval for Kerendia with a hyperkalemia safety note, saw Amundi cross a 3% voting threshold, and its Leaps/Robigo arm closed Series A for engineered crop biologics.
: Apollo-led funds and KKR invested €3bn for minority stakes in a new vehicle holding Bayer AG’s long-acting reversible contraceptives unit; Bayer keeps majority ownership and operational control.
: Bayer (BAYN) wins FDA approval for Kerendia (finerenone) in adults with CKD linked to type 1 diabetes. Label notes reduced UACR; safety flag: hyperkalemia—monitor potassium and eGFR.
: Amundi S.A. reported crossing the 3% voting rights threshold in Bayer AG (BAYN) as of 14 Sept 2026; notification filed under German disclosure rules around 17–18 Sept 2026.
: Bayer (BAYN) unit Leaps and Robigo closed a Series A to fund engineered crop biologicals, backing R&D and commercialization to protect yields and cut grower costs.
